title: The Book of Basketball: The NBA According to The Sports Guy
author: Bill Simmons (foreword Malcolm Gladwell)
price_band: varies — Waterstones pb/hc snippets ~£15–21 (retailer; not Amazon)
why_comparable: Seed: the fan-intellectual NBA history/argument bible Glen’s desk is measured against — maximal Simmons voice vs Taylor’s cognitive-analytics and Greene’s interdisciplinary watch-guide.
format_notes: hardcover (2009); paperback updated reprint ISBN 9780345520104; Kindle

title: Thinking Basketball
author: Ben Taylor
price_band: varies — Amazon.com paperback listed (price not re-scraped live UK); ASIN 1532968175
why_comparable: Seed: cognitive-bias + possession-value primer that sits opposite Simmons’ anecdote-heavy Hall of Fame arguing — shorter, myth-busting, YouTube-adjacent analytics literacy.

title: How to Watch Basketball Like a Genius: What Game Designers, Economists, Ballet Choreographers, and Theoretical Astrophysicists Reveal About the Greatest Game on Earth
author: Nick Greene
price_band: £8–15 pb (LoveReading UK £12.99 / £11.69; Abrams US list $18 pb)
why_comparable: Seed: verified Nick Greene (not a different author) — interdisciplinary ‘how to see the game’ adjacent to Simmons entertainment and Taylor analysis, lighter on box-score math.

title: Basketball on Paper: Rules and Tools for Performance Analysis
author: Dean Oliver
price_band: varies — publisher pb/ebook; no live Amazon price scraped
why_comparable: Foundational four-factors / per-possession bible — denser and more coach-facing than Thinking Basketball, the technical ancestor of modern ‘smart fan’ analytics books.

title: Sprawlball: A Visual Tour of the New Era of the NBA
author: Kirk Goldsberry
price_band: varies — amazon.co.uk product URL known; live star/price GAP (blocked/unverified)
why_comparable: Shot-chart visual analytics of the three-point era — sits with Thinking Basketball on ‘why the game looks like this,’ marketed explicitly for Simmons/FreeDarko readers.

title: The Midrange Theory: Basketball's Evolution In the Age of Analytics
author: Seth Partnow
price_band: varies — Triumph trade paper list $18.95 US (publisher page)
why_comparable: Team-side analytics literacy (draft/cap/RAPM context) — deeper front-office than Greene’s watch book, more applied than Oliver’s 2004 toolkit.

title: Seven Seconds or Less: My Season on the Bench with the Runnin' and Gunnin' Phoenix Suns
author: Jack McCallum
price_band: varies — used/new market; no live list price captured today
why_comparable: Embedded season chronicle of pace-and-space ancestors — narrative access like Simmons storytelling, documenting the offense that later analytics books explain.

title: Eleven Rings: The Soul of Success
author: Phil Jackson; Hugh Delehanty
price_band: varies — widely reprinted pb/Kindle; Amazon stars GAP today
why_comparable: Last Dance–adjacent coach memoir (Bulls/Lakers) — leadership/triangle culture vs Simmons’ ranking essays or Taylor’s bias chapters; popular coaching popularization.

title: Scorecasting: The Hidden Influences Behind How Sports Are Played and Games Are Won
author: Tobias J. Moskowitz; L. Jon Wertheim
price_band: varies — Penguin Random House pb ISBN 9780307591807; Amazon price GAP
why_comparable: Multi-sport Moneyball-adjacent behavioral econ (home refs, clutch myths) — shares Thinking Basketball’s bias-debunking lane, less basketball-only than Oliver/Goldsberry.

title: The Victory Machine: The Making and Unmaking of the Warriors Dynasty
author: Ethan Sherwood Strauss
price_band: varies — Hachette pb 9781541736221; Amazon price GAP
why_comparable: Modern dynasty reportage (Warriors FO/KD era) — journalistic narrative companion to Sprawlball’s on-court analytics of the same revolution.

title: Blood in the Garden: The Flagrant History of the 1990s New York Knicks
author: Chris Herring
price_band: varies — S&S hc/pb; Amazon price GAP
why_comparable: Oral-history team era book — cultural/physical ’90s Knicks for readers who want Simmons-era nostalgia with reported depth rather than rankings.

title: The City Game: Basketball from the Garden to the Playgrounds
author: Pete Axthelm
publisher: Bison Books / University of Nebraska Press (reprint); originally Harper & Row
price_band: varies — Nebraska reprint pb; used market common
why_comparable: Classic NYC playground-to-Garden cultural history (user’s ‘City Game’ ask; youth ‘Triple Threat’ novels excluded as off-desk) — ancestor of smart fan cultural writing, not analytics.

title: Showtime: Magic, Kareem, Riley, and the Los Angeles Lakers Dynasty of the 1980s
author: Jeff Pearlman
price_band: varies — PRH paperback 9781592408870; Amazon price GAP
why_comparable: Big oral-history dynasty narrative — Showtime Lakers for Simmons-style era immersion without the ranking thesis of Book of Basketball.

title: Dream Team: How Michael, Magic, Larry, Charles, and the Greatest Team of All Time Conquered the World and Changed the Game of Basketball Forever
author: Jack McCallum
price_band: varies — PRH pb 9780345520494; Amazon price GAP
why_comparable: 1992 Olympics origin myth reporting — popular history adjacent to Last Dance / Dream Team lore that Simmons readers already argue about.

title: The Breaks of the Game
author: David Halberstam
price_band: varies — reprint pb 9781401309725 common; Amazon price GAP
why_comparable: Canonical embedded NBA season (1979–80 Trail Blazers) — the literary bar for longform basketball narrative that Simmons-era books still echo.

title: When the Game Was Ours
author: Larry Bird; Earvin "Magic" Johnson; Jackie MacMullan
price_band: varies — widely available pb; Amazon price GAP
why_comparable: Rivalry memoir (Bird–Magic) — player-voice history that pairs with Dream Team / Showtime for ’80s desk reading without analytics.
format_notes: hardcover 2009 ISBN 9780547225470; Mariner paperback 2010 ISBN 9780547394589; audiobook

title: Basketball (and Other Things): A Collection of Questions Asked, Answered, Illustrated
author: Shea Serrano
price_band: varies — Abrams editions; Amazon price GAP
why_comparable: Illustrated debate-essay watch companion — closer to Simmons humor/ranking energy and Greene’s approachable watch desk than to Oliver’s math.

title: FreeDarko Presents: The Macrophenomenal Pro Basketball Almanac: Styles, Stats, and Stars in Today's Game
author: Bethlehem Shoals and FreeDarko collective
price_band: varies — often OOP/used; Amazon price GAP
why_comparable: Proto–smart-fan aesthetic/stats almanac — stylistic ancestor Sprawlball name-checks; between Simmons culture and early analytics vernacular.

title: There's Always This Year: On Basketball and Ascension
author: Hanif Abdurraqib
price_band: varies — Random House hc/pb; Amazon price GAP
why_comparable: Literary cultural essay on fandom/ascension (Cleveland/LeBron orbit) — expands the desk beyond box scores into the cultural lane Greene and Simmons also touch.
